basis: Hydranencephaly and a structural diaphragmatic defect define the syndrome; common pulmonary hypoplasia is not established by the supplied syndrome evidence.

decisions.pulmonary: none: pulmonary hypoplasia is not documented for this syndrome; associated pulmonary hypertension is vascular and has no stated frequency.

basis: Cryptophthalmos, cutaneous syndactyly and urinary anomalies are major criteria; airway lesions occur in 2/2. Hearing loss, clefts and seizures (1/2 each) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: laryngeal stenosis in 2/2 and pulmonary hyperplasia in 2/3 establish common structural airway/lung involvement; primary axes capped at three.
decisions.renal: primary: renal and urinary tract malformations are major Fraser diagnostic criteria; renal malformations occur in roughly 40%.
decisions.dermatologic: primary: cutaneous syndactyly is a major diagnostic criterion and represents congenital skin fusion.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: the recorded syndactyly is explicitly cutaneous; independent bone, joint or muscle disease is not established.

basis: Chronic frontal sinus inflammation affects the upper airway; mixed infectious, allergic and obstructive causes do not establish a specific immune or infectious mechanism.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: chronic inflammation alone does not establish an infectious or immune-mediated disease; this etiologically mixed concept includes obstructive causes.

basis: EBV infects lymphocytes with lymphoid proliferation; hepatic inflammation with hepatocellular injury occurs in ~80-90%. Transient pharyngitis does not establish lasting airway damage.

decisions.hepatic: involved: EBV-associated hepatic inflammation and hepatocellular injury occur in ~80-90%, as part of the acute disease rather than a later disease risk.
decisions.pulmonary: none: pharyngitis is a transient manifestation; lasting airway damage is not common, and serious airway obstruction is a minority complication.

basis: Neurologic dysfunction, contractures/myopathy and cardiomyopathy characterize the core spectrum; cataract, deafness and renal stones lack established common frequencies.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: cardiomyopathy is a core manifestation in the multisystem disease definition, alongside neurologic and skeletal muscle involvement.

basis: Interferon-mediated disease; destructive AGS-type encephalopathy and chronic chilblain skin injury each affect >30% of the reported SAMHD1 spectrum, despite skin-only presentations.

decisions.neurologic: involved: AGS5 is a major SAMHD1 presentation; destructive encephalopathy affects >30% of the usual reported spectrum, although chilblain-only cases lack it.

basis: Hepatic ductal-plate malformation and fibro-obliterative cholangiopathy define this disorder; congestive splenomegaly does not establish blood-organ damage.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: ZFYVE19 disease is a developmental cholangiopathy/ciliopathy; the broad bilirubin-metabolism ancestor does not establish an intrinsic metabolic defect.

basis: Cerebellar degeneration and axonal neuropathy define disease; amyotrophy (4/4) reflects denervation rather than direct muscle disease. Eye movement abnormalities are neurologic.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: distal amyotrophy occurs in 4/4 but is secondary to axonal denervation; direct skeletal muscle disease is not established.

basis: Generalized fibrous bone disease with characteristic hypophosphatemia; the discordant myelofibrosis ancestor alone does not establish marrow fibrosis or blood-cell dysfunction.

decisions.haematologic: none: the described phenotype supports skeletal fibrous dysplasia; no marrow fibrosis or blood-cell disorder is demonstrated beyond a discordant ontology parent.

basis: T-B+ SCID entails profound T-cell lymphopenia and impaired adaptive immunity; respiratory, oral and ear infections are separately diagnosed consequences.

decisions.haematologic: primary: profound T-cell lymphopenia defines T-B+ SCID, with reduced lymphocyte count in 1/1 annotated patient; this directly affects blood cells.
